witness_description: No witness found. Under the standard reading of the quoted claim (C = the undirected cycle graph C_k on k vertices with k edges), every subset of k-1 edges of C_k, for every k in 3..16, was verified by exact integer union-find and BFS to be a spanning tree of C_k (spans all k vertices, connected, acyclic) with every ordered pair of vertices mutually reachable. 133 subsets checked in total; none violates the claim.
refutation_explanation: The claim was not refuted. It is in fact provable in general under this reading: C_k has exactly k edges, so a subset of k-1 edges omits exactly one edge, leaving a Hamiltonian path on all k vertices, which is a spanning tree and preserves undirected reachability between all pairs. Caveats: the quote defines neither C nor k; the search adopts the only dimensionally consistent standard reading (C a k-vertex, k-edge cycle). If the surrounding proof intended C as a DIRECTED cycle with 'reachability' meaning strong connectivity, the claim would fail (removing any arc of a directed k-cycle destroys strong connectivity), but the quoted text says 'spanning tree', which is an undirected notion, and no directedness is stated in the record, so that variant was not treated as the claim.
search_space: For every k in 3..16: all C(k, k-1) = k subsets of size k-1 of the k edges {i,(i+1) mod k} of the undirected cycle C_k, enumerated in fixed lexicographic order via itertools.combinations (133 subsets total). Each subset checked exactly (Python ints only) for: spanning all vertices, connectivity, acyclicity, and all-ordered-pairs reachability.
